name: Puerto Baquerizo Moreno
referenceLabel: Puerto Baquerizo Moreno · San Cristóbal Island
referenceNote: Coastal town on San Cristóbal; this point does not represent the island's highlands or other Galápagos islands. Climate is fetched for this point. Peak and shoulder months inherit the old Galápagos regional estimates, not measured local crowds.

name: Puerto Villamil
referenceNote: Coastal town on Isabela; this point does not represent the island's volcanic highlands or other Galápagos islands. Climate is fetched for this point. Peak and shoulder months inherit the old Galápagos regional estimates, not measured local crowds.

name: Panaji
referenceNote: Panaji (also called Panjim) is the city reference point near the Mandovi estuary; it does not represent every Goa beach or the inland hills. Peak and shoulder months inherit the old Goa regional estimates, not measured local crowds.

name: Palolem
referenceNote: Palolem's populated coastal locality is the reference point, not the whole state of Goa. A regional climate grid may still smooth beach and inland differences. Peak and shoulder months inherit the old Goa regional estimates, not measured local crowds.

name: El Chaltén
referenceNote: The reference point is El Chaltén town in Santa Cruz, not Fitz Roy's summit, mountain trails or all Patagonia. Climate grids can smooth steep local elevation changes. Peak and shoulder months inherit the old Patagonia regional estimates, not measured local crowds.

name: Puerto Natales
referenceNote: The reference point is Puerto Natales town by the Última Esperanza fjord, not Torres del Paine, mountain trails or all Patagonia. Peak and shoulder months inherit the old Patagonia regional estimates, not measured local crowds.

name: Sanur
referenceNote: Sanur's coastal populated place is the reference point; it does not represent inland Bali or mountain resorts. Regional grids may not distinguish nearby coastal and inland locations. Peak and shoulder months inherit the existing Bali regional estimates, not measured local crowds.

name: Ubud
referenceNote: Ubud town in inland Gianyar is the reference point, not the whole district or the coastal Denpasar anchor. Regional grids can smooth local elevation and rainfall differences. Peak and shoulder months inherit the existing Bali regional estimates, not measured local crowds.

name: Puerto de la Cruz
referenceLabel: Puerto de la Cruz · north-coast Tenerife
referenceNote: The reference point is the coastal town on Tenerife's north side, not the island as a whole or the existing El Médano anchor. Regional grids may smooth coast and slope differences. Peak and shoulder months inherit the existing Tenerife regional estimates, not measured local crowds.

name: La Orotava
referenceLabel: La Orotava town · inland north Tenerife
referenceNote: La Orotava town is the reference point, not the municipality's high mountain terrain or Teide summit. Regional grids can smooth the sharp elevation change from the nearby coast. Peak and shoulder months inherit the existing Tenerife regional estimates, not measured local crowds.

name: Maafushi
referenceNote: The reference point is the inhabited coral island of Maafushi in Kaafu Atoll, not all Maldives islands. Its 1991–2020 daily climate grid series is identical to the Malé reference; island and beach differences are unresolved. Peak and shoulder months inherit the old Maldives regional estimates, not measured local crowds.

name: Dhigurah
referenceNote: The reference point is Dhigurah's inhabited village in South Ari Atoll, as identified by Visit Maldives, not the whole atoll or the Maldives. Regional grid estimates cannot resolve individual beaches, reefs or lagoons. Peak and shoulder months inherit the old Maldives regional estimates, not measured local crowds.
